title: Шеф заперт в холодильнике  (The Chef Locked in the Walk-in Fridge)

segments.t: Hoping the cold temperature will slow down the fugu toxin and keep Chef Barinov from getting behind the wheel, Fedya tricks him into stepping inside the walk-in refrigerator. Leaving him a crate of cognac so he will not freeze, the cooks bolt the heavy door shut.
Шеф, я что-то не могу разобраться.
Как ты мог этого не знать?
Федя, здесь же на коробке написано.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
Шеф, я что-то не могу разобраться.
'Chef, I cannot seem to figure this out.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'chef', while 'to deal with' completes the thought.
'Oh, Fyodor, Fyodor.' The grammar packs 'oh' and 'Fyodor' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Which means.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'and' and finishing on 'so'. Fedya answers right away.
Как ты мог этого не знать?
'How could you not know that?' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'could' to negate the statement.
'He is going to freeze in there.' The meaning hinges on 'he' working together with 'will freeze' in spoken Russian.
'I left him a crate of cognac.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'would keep' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'He will not freeze.' In Russian, the idea of 'not' flows naturally into 'will freeze' without extra filler words.
'That is my cognac.' In Russian, the idea of 'this' flows naturally into 'cognac' without extra filler words.
'Better the cognac than...' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'better' before landing on 'what'. Fedya answers right away.
Федя, здесь же на коробке написано.
'Fedya, it is written right here on the box.' The grammar packs 'Fedya' and 'is written' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Fedya, what kind of joke is this?' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'Fedya', while 'joke' completes the thought.
'Fedya, what is going on?' Fedya raises the pitch on 'is going on' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Come on, open up right now!' The grammar packs 'and' and 'open' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
Шеф, я что-то не могу разобраться.
Как ты мог этого не знать?
Федя, здесь же на коробке написано.
